findings.reason: as written the node fails an impossible gate on any correct repair and would report a miss, or pass a meaningless one; the bound must be restated (for example "at most base's median", or the 30 s deadline §31's Why names), and the report's "base" arm fixed to a named revision, since §31's own two sentences use "base" for both §19's base and "the base tree" of the negative control.
findings.text: the done-when requires three fresh-process builds at head and at base with "head's median is at most base's minus 30 s", but §31's Why and §25's landed evidence both put that base (`d249200c7`) at 40.8 s wall, so the bound demands head ≤ ~10.8 s while the repair only removes the ~41 s of redundant 285 MB store rewrites (head 82.2 s → about base's 40.8 s), and the fastest revision §25 measured anywhere is the pre-§19 arm at 22.7 s

findings.reason: with no sequence declared the scheduler may run §31 beside §26 or §29 on the same two files, which the plan's one-writer-per-file convention exists to prevent, and §31 changes when the store is flushed — exactly the state §26's fresh-process read consumes.
findings.text: §31's write paths are `reckon/metadata_index.py` and `reckon/serve.py`, and §26 (`reckon/serve.py`, `reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/metadata_index.py`) and §29 (`reckon/serve.py`, `reckon/resources.py`, `reckon/metadata_index.py`, `reckon/sprint_liveness.py`) write the same two files, yet §31 states no ordering while every neighbouring section does (§29 "Build it after §26", §30 "Build it after §29", §28 "Build it after §22")

findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching the open followup's own invocation re-runs §25 instead of the §26 that remains, and the plan's own precedent (f-araiid-019 resolved at §19's landing, f-araiid-017 at §17's) is that the chain is re-pointed at each landing; it should name §26 (and §31, the repair §25 filed).
findings.text: the open followup `f-araiid-022` has `data-recommends-skill="/reckon-build a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline §25"` and is the only open chain into §26 to §27, but §25 is now `data-status="done"`, so the recommended invocation names a completed section

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `runs.parse_stream_line` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:1871`), `runs.watch_stream_path` (re-exported at `reckon/crew/runs.py:3388`), `sprint_liveness._recorded_states` (`reckon/sprint_liveness.py:57`), `mcp_views._recorded_live_run_classifications` (`reckon/mcp_views.py:1806`), `metadata_index.record_discovery` (call site `reckon/serve.py:2309`, def `reckon/metadata_index.py:818`), `_store_persisted` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:1046`) and `_store.write_json_atomically` (`reckon/_store.py:531`) all resolve, and the §25 evidence link `#s25-store-build-excess` resolves in the landed archive.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §30 and §31 each name a test, a count, and a negative control against a copy of the base tree, and each control can fail (base parses the watch stream three times; base calls `_store_persisted` once per discovered document).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both nodes write their gate and control logs under the run directory, not node-local scratch; §31's `sbatch --wait` job is the one partition exception, and its logs land on GPFS.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or comment; §30's one review-history sentence ("The plan review corrected the first draft") is the same shape a prior review declined on §28 and carries no mechanism the node must honour, so it does not change the plan.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §31's report bound ("head's median is at most base's minus 30 s") cannot be met by the section's own mechanism against the base its Why names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §30 delivers one shared parse of the project watch stream; §31 delivers one store write per discovery pass, each with its own measure.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §31 writes `reckon/serve.py` and `reckon/metadata_index.py`, the same two files §26 and §29 write, and declares no ordering; the open followup `f-araiid-022` still recommends §25, which is now `done`.
